beats.narration_text: Hola, this is Liam, in for Bear. This is how Walker is meant to be asked: hand it a game design document, get back a playable Godot project. The prompt on screen is a reconstruction, not a transcript, because this game was rebuilt first, and its document came after.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about a first-person survival-crafting game — wake in an abandoned valley, gather sticks, gold and stone, craft an axe and a campfire, and survive one night until dawn — into a playable Godot project.
props.runningText: illustrative reconstruction — not the historical prompt
output: What happened: a partial Unity prototype was rebuilt in Godot first.
GDD.md was written afterwards, from the evidence.

show.event: ClaudeComposerAsk: The Design Document

beats.narration_text: Fantasy Survival Crafting came before its design document. It rebuilds a Unity prototype that had no scenes, no audio and no way to win, and completes it into one night of survival. The document was written last, and nothing in it is signed off.

props.text:
Fantasy Survival Crafting
was built from its GDD.
Nothing is signed off.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant writer: text is typed on screen over the narration, so mid-beat samples legitimately show a partial page. The finished six-line text fills the safe area and holds for the last 1.5 s.

beats.narration_text: The document opens by separating six kinds of claim: recovered from the Unity code, invented for the rebuild, built, observed, proposed, or still waiting on a person. Built is large: twenty-three scripts and three shaders. Observed: forty-two of the game's own checks, and seventy-four more in this film's three scripted takes. Human playtests: zero.

beats.narration_text: The vision is a proposal: wake in an abandoned valley, gather and craft through one afternoon, keep a fire burning until dawn. Who it's for is left open on purpose. The three pillars are read off the code: every tool comes from the land, the clock is the enemy, and your body keeps score.

portrait_card.reason: native 9:16 large-type card; shared 916 board fine print is below the GATE T portrait floor

show.event: portrait card: A Vision Nobody Signed

beats.narration_text: Here's the core loop on the real build, played by a script, not a person. Look at a stick and press E. Craft the axe. Fell a pine in four swings. Then the campfire goes down by the lake. Every step is a cut from the same morning's take, in order.

beats.narration_text: Four experience goals, all proposed, each with a test a person has to run. The captures can only hint. The scripted run placed its fire at twelve twenty-five, more than seven hours before dark, but it already knew the map. And food did matter: calories fell from a hundred to thirty-five by early afternoon, and three meals brought them back.

beats.narration_text: Mechanics start with movement, and an honest retune. Unity moved the player at twelve metres a second with a three-metre jump. The rebuild keeps the gravity and the jump formula, but walks at five and a half, sprints at eight and a half, and jumps one point two metres, tuned for a ten-minute session.

portrait_card.reason: native 9:16 large-type card; shared 916 board fine print is below the GATE T portrait floor

show.event: portrait card: Same Physics, Slower Feet

beats.narration_text: Pickup and crafting, in play. The centre of the screen is the selector: the stick's name appears, E collects it, and a popup confirms. Later, the crafting screen shows the axe's recipe, three gold and three sticks, both owned, so the Craft button appears. One click, and press one to equip it.

beats.narration_text: Chopping and hunting are new, but Unity hinted at them: its sound manager declared a tool-swing and a chop sound that no script ever played. The rebuild uses them. Pines take four hits and drop two logs. Rabbits wander like Unity's AI, and bolt when you come within five metres.

beats.narration_text: Four swings, four shakes, and the pine topples away from the player. Then a rabbit, in motion, which the document itself says nobody had reviewed until now. It runs, the axe connects, it plays its death clip, and leaves meat.

beats.narration_text: The clock is the design's spine. Day runs at twenty-four seconds per game hour, night at twelve, and the game starts at half past seven. A placed fire warms you within nine metres. Resting there runs time nine times faster. And victory needs both: dawn, and part of the night spent beside your fire.

beats.narration_text: One rule the document doesn't list. Facing the lake, the fire is refused: you can't build a fire in the water, because its spot lands two and a half metres ahead. A few steps inland, the same right-click lights it.

beats.narration_text: Night falls at eight, and the fire keeps the cold away. E at the fire rests, and the clock races. At dawn: dawn breaks, day two, sixteen items, two trees, one rabbit.

beats.narration_text: Survival stats follow Unity's, with added pressure. Water drops every five seconds. Idle time burns calories too. An empty stat costs one health a second, the night cold one every one point four, and you heal only when well fed. All of these rates are proposed, pending a human playtest.

beats.narration_text: Cooking needs a fire nearby, and now there is one. Rabbit meat becomes cooked meat. In the inventory, hover an item for its description, drag one to the last slot, and right-click to eat: cooked meat, an apple, a mushroom. Calories go from thirty-five back to a hundred.

beats.narration_text: Two more decisions the rebuild made on its own. Dropping an item onto a full slot swaps the two, where Unity left it in place. And the save menu Unity drew, with no code behind it, now writes one save slot, with Load Game on the main menu and Load Save on the defeat screen.

beats.narration_text: The failure path, from the night save. Walk away from the fire, and the cold sets in: a blue overlay and a warning. The N key, Unity's own debug damage, speeds it along. Lost to the wilds. Load Save puts you back beside the fire.

beats.narration_text: The world is authored: a procedural valley two hundred and sixty metres across, ringed by mountains, with a lake, a village and three pine groves. Every model comes from the source asset packs, repaired at load time. Every sound was synthesized, because the source folders had none.

portrait_card.reason: native 9:16 large-type card; shared 916 board fine print is below the GATE T portrait floor

show.event: portrait card: A Valley From Asset Packs

beats.narration_text: Under the hood, every scene is thin. The game scene file is six lines, and the running valley holds nearly two thousand nodes, all built in code. Out of scope, by decision: more save slots, more nights, building beyond the fire, enemies and weather.

portrait_card.reason: native 9:16 large-type card; shared 916 board fine print is below the GATE T portrait floor
portrait_card.title: Six Lines, Two Thousand Nodes

show.event: portrait card: Six Lines, Two Thousand Nodes

beats.narration_text: The risks section is candid: nobody has played this by hand, and rabbit animation was only seen in stills. The film's captures close that second gap, and find one thing the document misses. Once a recipe uses your materials, the objective list still ticks them, but reads zero of three. Five open questions remain for a person.

portrait_card.reason: native 9:16 large-type card; shared 916 board fine print is below the GATE T portrait floor
portrait_card.title: What a Person Still Has to Decide

show.event: portrait card: What a Person Still Has to Decide

beats.narration_text: Verdict. This document organizes; it doesn't approve. The loop runs end to end in real input, from a new game to dawn and to defeat. The rebuild's own additions are clearly labelled. One small display bug slipped past every check. What's left is a person's call: the audience, the tuning, and whether one night is enough.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude with your own design document: Here is my game's design document. Pick one proposed experience goal. Rewrite it as a hypothesis with a test I can run with three players, and tell me which result would make me change the design. If no result would change your mind, it isn't a hypothesis yet. Liam, in for Bear.
